newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin Central buys rail lines.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin Central buys rail lines.

text.p: Wisconsin Central Ltd said it acquired more than 18 route miles of rail line serving Wausau and Hayward, Wis., from Union Pacific Corp.
Wisconsin Central Ltd, a unit of Wisconsin Central Transportation Corp, said it bought the track for $3.8 million, subject to certain final adjustments.
The transaction was approved April 17 by the U.S. Surface Transportation Board.

The Wausau trackage extends 10 miles from Wausau to Kelly, Wis., plus a two-mile branch line from Kelly to Schofield. The Hayward line extends six miles from Hayward to Hayward Junction, connecting with Wisconsin Central's main line between Chicago and Superior, Wis.
The two line segments serve 10 principal customers that generate about 12,300 carloads annually.
The two lines had been served by Union Pacific since June 1995, following its acquisition of the Chicago and NorthWestern.
Wisconsin Central, through its subsidiaries, operates approximately 3,000 route miles of railway serving Wisconsin, Illinois, Minnesota, Michigan's Upper Peninsula, and Ontario, Canada.
